review_excerpt_and_triage.source: User-provided decision/review excerpt, 2026-11-04; not an independent whole-paper audit.
review_excerpt_and_triage.verbatim: Specifically, the submission is below the acceptable criteria for presentation clarity and validity, leading to concerns about the paper's significance. As a result of its overly complex and dense writing, the underlying contribution is neither understandable nor convincing as a CHI paper. Furthermore, the evaluation lacks critical details such as comprehensive task description, and the comparison probes seem designed in a way that favors the proposed system rather than serving as fair and comparable baseline alternatives. Given that much of the system seems to rely on augmented reality, it is further unclear how the system would work in practice.
reviewer_concerns: Dense writing obscures contribution and significance
Comparison probes appear favorable to the proposed system rather than fair alternatives
Practical AR implementation and use unclear
review_excerpt_and_triage.agent_synthesis: These are actionable clarity, reporting, comparison and deployment concerns, not evidence that the entire direction is worthless. The excerpt alone does not establish that every criticism is correct or that reviewer preference explains rejection.
review_excerpt_and_triage.probe_baseline_distinction: Exploratory probes may intentionally differ when used to elicit interpretations, provided rationale and claim limits are clear. Comparative superiority claims require credible, appropriately matched baselines and attention to order, learning and bundled differences. Do not retroactively relabel the executed study.
review_excerpt_and_triage.vr_ar_ambiguity: Local records describe a VR evaluation; the excerpt discusses reliance on AR. Audit manuscript descriptions of implemented prototype, evaluation and deployment vision before attributing misunderstanding to either author or reviewer.

critical_alternatives: A good common expression may be sufficient.

User configuration or explicit asking may outperform automatic inference.
Shared history may create misleading expectations rather than improve communication.
More accurate communication may reduce closeness while improving appropriate expectations.
Negotiation or correction may cost more effort than it saves.
